Avoid unnecessary travel at night, in severe weather, or when injury or fatigue is worsening. For a crossing, look for a wide shallow section away from rapids, falls, and hazards downstream. Unbuckle pack waist and chest straps, face upstream, and use a sturdy pole only when the crossing is clearly manageable. Turn back when water is swift, deep, rising, very cold, or the exit cannot be seen; never tie yourself to a crossing rope.
